name: Azaryahu
overview: Azaryahu was a male member of the tribe of Judah, identified uniquely as the son of Jehoshaphat. His mention in Scripture is brief, with no additional personal notes or details provided beyond his lineage. This establishes him within the Davidic line, reflecting his tribal and familial heritage.
namesAndTitles: The name Azaryahu means 'YHWH has helped,' indicating a recognition of divine assistance. This proper name, as recorded in 2 Chronicles 21:2, reflects the theocentric nature typical of Hebrew names, though it was not explicitly given by God.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records Azaryahu as the son of Jehoshaphat. Additionally, it is inferred that he was killed by Jehoram, another figure mentioned in the same passage. Beyond these relationships, no further family connections are detailed in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Azaryahu's significance lies primarily in his place within the royal lineage of Judah as Jehoshaphat's son. His death at the hands of Jehoram, as inferred from the text, situates him within the turbulent history of Judah's monarchy. Though not extensively detailed, his presence contributes to the understanding of the dynastic struggles recorded in 2 Chronicles.
